skill.name: testing-gate
skill.description: Verifies whether a feature has meaningful tests for critical paths, then returns a pass or warning without blocking progress.
skill.summary: Guides testing checks for feature work with practical warnings and mentoring prompts.
skill.author: DanielPodolsky

security_audit.summary: All ten static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, response templates, and ordinary testing guidance. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, network access, or instructions to execute commands.

static_findings.snippet: > "What tests did you write for this feature?"
| Interview-Ready | Full pyramid | Unit + Integration + E2E for critical flows |
- "What percentage coverage did you achieve?" (for resume)

finding_verdicts.reason: The matched text is an inline Markdown example of a weak test assertion, not Ruby or shell execution. It does not tell the agent to run a command.
The matched backticks open a Markdown response template for a passing test gate. The block contains user-facing text, not executable shell or Ruby code.
The matched backticks close a Markdown response template. There is no command invocation, interpolation, or instruction to execute the block.
The matched backticks open a Markdown warning template about missing tests. The content is mentoring prose and does not perform external command execution.
The matched backticks close the no-tests warning template. This is documentation syntax and contains no executable command path.
The matched backticks open a Markdown template for weak-test feedback. The block is sample output text, not shell or Ruby execution.
The line asks the learner what tests they wrote for a feature. It is a normal review question, not system reconnaissance.
The line is a placeholder asking the assistant to name a testing strength. It does not request environment, host, credential, or system details.
The line describes desired test-suite coverage levels, including unit, integration, and end-to-end tests. It is not an attempt to enumerate system information.
The line asks about test coverage percentage for resume discussion. It concerns project test quality, not system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Teams often miss tests for critical paths during fast reviews. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused testing checks.
actual_capabilities: Asks structured questions about test existence, coverage strategy, and test quality.
Classifies outcomes as pass or warning based on the provided testing evidence.
Provides response templates for passing tests, missing tests, and weak tests.
Explains what a strong test suite should cover across feature complexity levels.
Offers stack-specific testing hints for React, Next.js, backend APIs, and Python.
Connects testing work to interview and portfolio discussion points.
limitations: Does not run test suites or collect coverage metrics automatically.
Depends on the learner or agent to provide accurate project context.
Uses warnings instead of hard blocking, so weak coverage can still proceed.
Focuses on testing habits and review discussion, not full quality assurance.

use_cases.title: Mentor Junior Developers
use_cases.description: Guide learners to explain what their tests prove before moving to code review.

use_cases.title: Review Feature Readiness
use_cases.description: Check whether a feature has meaningful tests for happy paths, edge cases, and errors.

use_cases.title: Prepare Portfolio Projects
use_cases.description: Help developers identify testing work they can discuss in interviews and project writeups.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Test Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing gate for this feature. Ask what tests exist, what they prove, and whether any critical path is missing.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Weak Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: A learner has tests, but coverage seems shallow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these tests with the testing gate. Identify the weakest coverage area and suggest one practical improvement without blocking progress.

prompt_templates.title: Stack-Specific Guidance
prompt_templates.scenario: A reviewer wants advice matched to the project stack.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the testing gate to this project stack. Recommend suitable test types and one next test for the most important behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Interview-Ready Assessment
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for portfolio or interview preparation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing gate to assess whether this feature has interview-ready testing evidence. Summarize strengths, gaps, and a concise interview talking point.

output_examples.input: A feature includes unit tests for the happy path and one edge case.
output_examples.output: Testing gate passed. The review highlights covered behavior, names a key strength, and suggests one future improvement.

output_examples.input: A feature has no tests because the learner ran out of time.
output_examples.output: Testing gate warning. The response explains why tests matter, asks what should be tested next, and allows review to continue.

output_examples.input: A feature has tests, but they only check implementation details.
output_examples.output: Testing gate warning. The feedback explains the quality issue and suggests testing user-visible behavior instead.

best_practices: Ask for the most important test before judging overall coverage.
Tie feedback to observable behavior, not implementation details.
Suggest one realistic next test when coverage is missing or weak.
anti_patterns: Treating missing tests as a hard blocker when the gate defines warnings.
Accepting placeholder tests that do not verify real behavior.
Focusing only on coverage percentage without discussing critical paths.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides review questions and feedback, but it does not execute test commands.

faq.question: Can this skill block a feature from completion?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed to warn and encourage, not to block completion.

faq.question: What test types does it encourage?
faq.answer: It encourages happy path tests, edge case tests, error state tests, and critical flow coverage.

faq.question: Is this useful for junior developers?
faq.answer: Yes. The prompts help juniors explain testing decisions and build repeatable testing habits.

faq.question: Does it support specific frameworks?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for React, Next.js, backend APIs, and Python testing tools.

faq.question: How should reviewers use the warnings?
faq.answer: Use warnings to document risk and suggest the next useful test, while still allowing progress.
